Definition: from G1418 and a presumed derivative of G2059; difficult of explanation:--hard to be uttered.
BiblicalUsage: Hard to explain, hard to interpret, as the writer of Hebrews says there is much to say about Melchizedek, but it is hard to utter because the hearers are dull of hearing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe some truth is hard to explain only because my ears are dull, and the cure is to grow up into the solid food of the word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
